mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 9.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.5% over a 3-month period, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong aggregate demand, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100) following a recession, the S&P 500 tends to rebound as the market anticipates a supply-side recovery, producing positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 100 and the economy is in a post-recession phase, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1 growth rate above 1.0% annually) signals robust economic activity that supports corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.0% annually, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% in a 3-month window, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% over a 3-month period, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and increase in employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 8.5%), a monthly decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor conditions that boost consumer confidence and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 8.5% and UNRATE declines month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
